sources.title: EPA: Homeowners and Consumers Frequently Asked Questions
sources.method: Read current full primary source in native web research and verify supported claims
sources.claim: EPA does not require homeowners to replace existing HCFC22 equipment; existing equipment can still be serviced. Request appropriate certified technicians and repair of leaks rather than repeated topping off.

faq.q: Does an AC older than ten years have to be replaced before selling?
faq.a: Age alone does not establish that. ENERGY STAR identifies older equipment as a reason to consider a professional evaluation. The actual condition, proposed repair, buyer requirements and your sale strategy still matter.

faq.q: Does the R-22 phaseout automatically mean my existing AC must be replaced?
faq.a: No. EPA says homeowners are not required to replace existing HCFC-22 equipment and that existing systems can continue to be serviced. Ask a qualified technician about the actual system, repair options and availability rather than assuming the phaseout decides the sale.

faq.q: Will a new AC add its full cost to my selling price?
faq.a: There is no guarantee. Compare realistic proposals and the work, selling costs and time involved. Equipment efficiency information is not evidence of a particular increase in your house-sale proceeds.

faq.q: Can Cash As-Is review a house before AC replacement?
faq.a: Yes. Describe how the system is operating, what a technician found and what remains uncertain. Cash As-Is can evaluate the property in its present condition without requiring you to replace the AC for our purchase.
